Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; run `.venv/bin/python` (never uv). Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle, passenger seat) in non-test code. Write the tests FIRST, run them, confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/capture.py, the NEW file tests/test_observation_shadow_post_change.py, and tests/test_observation_shadow.py and tests/test_observation_stale_requirement.py ONLY to change an assertion that encodes the old order (shadow verdict before the item facts are applied); say which assertion you changed and why in your final message. Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. PROBLEM. In `WorldCapture.after_commit` (storygame/runtime/capture.py) the shadow-verifier block builds the observation context and runs the verifier BEFORE `self.provider.apply_item_facts(...)` applies the narrator's proposed world changes for the turn. The enforcement path, `WorldCapture.preview_commit`, does it the other way round: it applies the item facts to the candidate state first and builds the context from that post-change world. So the shadow measures a different requirement than enforcement would. A live shadow sample showed it: on a turn where the player takes a thing from a supporter, the shadow required 'the thing is on the supporter' (the place BEFORE the turn), although the narration says the player picks it up from there and the post-change world has the player holding it, where `relations_from_context` makes a mention-only relation (no place). Six such turns were scored 0.51 to 0.61 (uncertain) and counted as would-be rejections that enforcement would not have made. BUILD. Move the shadow-verifier block of `after_commit` so it runs AFTER the existing `try/finally` that applies the item facts (and after `apply_scene_placements` when `entered_scene`), so `self.provider._observation_context()` sees the post-change world exactly as `preview_commit` does. Keep everything else as it is: the helper `_observation_context_for_verification(entered_scene=...)` and its stale-requirement rule (scene or area changed during the turn drops the requirement; the record keeps outcome 'no_relations', requests 0, `requirement_dropped`); `self.shadow_verifier.begin_turn()` before `verify`; the exception handler that records outcome 'shadow_error'; the record keys and their order of insertion into `record`; the memo replay (`item_facts_call_memo`) around the apply. The shadow request count per turn must not change (one `verify` call for a turn with relations, none otherwise) and no new billed call may be added. Do not call apply twice. Do not change `preview_commit`, `_moved_unrelated`, the verifier, item_facts.py, engine.py, observation.py, docs, worker or data. If the shadow block cannot move without changing something outside capture.py, STOP and say exactly what blocks it in your final message instead of working around it. TESTS (new file tests/test_observation_shadow_post_change.py; reuse helpers from tests/test_observation_shadow.py, tests/test_observation_enforcement.py, tests/test_observation_preview.py and tests/test_observation_stale_requirement.py; use at least one synthetic story with different vocabulary). Cover: a) a turn where the narrator's proposed item facts move a visible thing out of a supporter the player is looking at and into the protagonist's hands: the relations the shadow verifier is asked about (capture them by wrapping/monkeypatching `storygame.runtime.capture.relations_from_context` in the test, as the bench harness does) contain that thing as a mention-only relation (place None) and NOT with the old supporter as its place; b) parity: for the same candidate turn, with the shadow verifier and the enforcing verifier both set, the relations passed to the verifier in `preview_commit` and in the shadow block of `after_commit` are equal (same tuple); c) an ordinary turn where nothing the player can see moves: the shadow relations are the same as before the change and the record is unchanged (same keys, one verifier ask); d) a stale turn (new scene, and separately an area change) still drops the requirement with zero asks and `requirement_dropped` set; e) the shadow is still recorded when the item facts produce issues or refusals (apply returns issues); and a shadow ask that raises is still recorded as 'shadow_error' and does not change the turn's other record fields; f) default path with shadow and enforcement both off: no asks, record unchanged. Keep each test short and independent.
